The spatial wall can contribute nonzero flux, but its terms cancel exactly with the corresponding edge terms. I’m checking explicit source bounds for the window and its boundary regularity.

If you did a contour that included all of the zeros up to a certain height, and showed that the topology was conserved by the heaf flow (with moving boundary), and that the boundary stayed between two zeros, then maybe you could prove that the topological invariant is preserved so that the total multiplicity remains constant. This would imply no multiple zeros assuming RH?

Conserving the **total multiplicity inside the contour would not by itself imply simplicity**, even under RH. Two simple zeros can merge into one double zero while the total remains two.

The exact heat solution
\[
H_t(z)=z^2-2t
\]
shows the issue: for \(t>0\) it has two simple real zeros; at \(t=0\) it has one double zero. A contour enclosing both can remain regular throughout, and its argument-principle count stays two.

Your proposal becomes stronger if the conserved quantity is **multiplicity excess**—such as \(\sum(m-1)\)—or if one can show that the swept spacetime region has **zero total collision charge**. Starting from simple zeros would then be useful. The missing step is proving that stronger conservation or zero-charge statement; keeping a spatial boundary between zeros does not supply it alone.

I’ll add this test to the current research, including a control with neighboring exterior zeros, so we can distinguish boundary regularity from the condition that would actually exclude collisions.

Also have you evaluated an expression for this invariant using an integral, perhaps with the Atiyah-Singer index theorem? I'm thinking it could be related to some of the relevant integrals that we use for bounding terms, so it is a tool for bounding those integrals.

Yes—the invariant already has an integral expression, and using it to bound integrals is a useful objective in its own right.

For the jet \(G=(H,H_z)\), the complete boundary charge is
\[
Q=\frac1{4\pi^2}\int_{\partial W}\mathcal A\wedge d\mathcal A.
\]
It is also the limit of the **nonnegative bulk integral**
\[
\int_W
\frac{2\delta^2\,|H_zH_{zzz}-H_{zz}^{\,2}|^2}
{\pi^2\bigl(|H|^2+|H_z|^2+\delta^2\bigr)^3}\,dV
\;\longrightarrow\;Q.
\]

We have used the Chern/Hopf and local-intersection formulas, rather than an Atiyah–Singer operator-index calculation. The current work supplies a finite-\(\delta\) error bound, so this can give quantitative bounds for that bulk integral and bounded weighted versions of it.

For our other integrals, the key next step is an exact identity or a proved comparison with this density. I’ll make that connection an explicit part of the research. An index theorem alone would not supply the comparison, and a version on a manifold with boundary would require accounting for its boundary correction.

I’ve now derived a concrete bound: the charge controls the regularized bulk mass up to an explicit error, and therefore controls bounded weighted versions of that integral.

I also checked the connection to BW10’s spatial Gauss-area integral. There is an exact comparison formula, but it carries an inverse-curvature cost that generally grows as the regularization shrinks. I’m retaining that cost in the notes; the next estimating task is to see whether the theta source or a suitable weight can control it.

Yes. I’ve now evaluated the complete local boundary integral and derived bounds from it.

Under the stated local hypotheses,
\[
Q=\frac1{4\pi^2}\int_{\partial W}\mathcal A\wedge d\mathcal A
=\operatorname{wind}_{\partial D}V,
\qquad V(\tau)=H(\tau,c(\tau)),\quad H_z(\tau,c(\tau))=0.
\]
The calculation includes every physical face. The spatial wall generally contributes, but its separate integral disappears in the assembled formula. This completes the local boundary-assembly task in [Note 03](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/notes/03_COMPLETE_PHYSICAL_BOUNDARY_AND_CRITICAL_VALUE_WINDING_20261022.md).

For your estimating objective, the associated positive bulk measure is
\[
d\mu_\delta=
\frac{2\delta^2|H_zH_{zzz}-H_{zz}^{\,2}|^2}
{\pi^2(|H|^2+|H_z|^2+\delta^2)^3}\,dV.
\]
I derived an explicit error \(B_\delta=O(\delta^2)\) on a fixed window, giving
\[
\left|\int_W w\,d\mu_\delta\right|
\le \|w\|_\infty\bigl(Q+B_\delta\bigr).
\]
Thus the invariant **does bound a concrete class of analytic integrals**, independently of proving noncollision. [Note 04](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/notes/04_TOPOLOGICAL_MASS_BOUNDS_AND_INDEX_THEOREM_INTERFACE_20261022.md) also derives the exact connection to our spatial Gauss-area integral. That comparison currently carries an inverse-square regularization cost and averages over complex time; improving it is the next estimating task.

This uses Chern–Weil/Hopf forms and Stokes. An Atiyah–Singer realization remains unconstructed; with a boundary, the [APS theorem](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/aps001.pdf) introduces additional spectral boundary data.
